Oliver: Heads-up: we need a decision on how saved views bind to routes vs models. Current ask from PM: allow a single saved view to be applied at route-level with a pinned_model override, without duplicating the saved view object. Thoughts?

Priya: Prefer not to duplicate. Suggest a `scoped_binding` layer that references saved_view + an override map. Example: ```json
{
  "saved_view_id": "sv_99",
  "scope": "route:r_12",
  "overrides": {"pinned_model": "m_7_quant", "filter_changes": {"q": "status:failed"}},
  "active_version": 3
}
```
This keeps saved_view canonical and allows route-specific staging.

Marco: API caution: we already surface saved_view versions in other endpoints. Adding a binding with `active_version` is fine. But we should store `staged_overrides` separately so we can have drafts. I don't want mutations to active binding to be immediately live.

Dana: UX: drafts are important. Users want to tweak filters and preview metrics before applying. Flow: Edit -> Save Draft -> Preview (with cost + telemetry sample) -> Apply (canary options). Show diff vs active view inline.

Nina: Telemetry: emit console.event = "saved_view.apply" with attrs {target_scope, saved_view_id, binding_id, user_id, rollout_mode, ramp}. For previews fire console.event = "saved_view.preview" including tokens_estimate_1h and sample_rate. Keep preview events separate from production apply events.

Oliver: Quota UI: when a saved view includes wide filters (e.g., no filters) and user applies to a heavy route warn them. We can call billing/estimator with a POST /estimate/tokens with payload: ```json
{"route_id":"r_12","saved_view_id":"sv_99","traffic_qps":100}
``` returns tokens_estimate_24h and cost_delta_cents. Show this in an apply modal with suggested throttles: 10qps, 50qps.

Priya: Implementation detail: staged_overrides should be immutable copies referencing a base saved_view_id and base_version. That way we can diff easily and support revert. Also allows audit trail.

Marco: Back-compat: migration path: create bindings for existing saved_views with scope=global and active_version set to current version. No changes to client unless they opt-in.

Dana: UX note: add small tag on saved view list that says "Bound to X routes" with hover to expand, and allow quick-open a route-bound draft preview.

infra-bot: deploy: ui-route-lens v3.0.0-canary deployed to prod-us-2 :rocket:

Nina: Regarding sampling: when previewing a canary set ramp < 100 and include `preview_sample_rate` in telemetry. For applies with rollout_mode=canary include `rollout_id` so our monitoring can group metrics.

Oliver: One last API debate: should the binding be its own top-level resource (/bindings) or nested under saved_views (/saved_views/:id/bindings)? I lean top-level since bindings can be long-lived objects with their own lifecycle.

Priya: top-level + index endpoints filtered by saved_view_id and scope. Easier to query from console and route services.

Marco: Agreed. Also add `last_applied_by`, `last_applied_at`, and `audit_log_url` to binding metadata.

Dana: I'll prototype the modal flow and the inline diff. Will include the cost preview and the revert affordance.

Oliver: Action items: Marco - design DB migration + binding model; Priya - API schema PR for /bindings and staged_overrides; Nina - telemetry event spec with sample payloads; Dana - UX mock and copy. Target: feature canary next week. Ping me when PRs are up.

Marco: I'll sketch migration notes today.

Priya: I'll open the API PR tomorrow AM.

Nina: I'll post the telemetry spec in #eng-ml and link here.

Dana: Dropping Figma link in 30m. :eyes: 

Oliver: Thanks team. If there are no objections we'll go with top-level bindings + staged_overrides and a cost-preview call before apply.

Priya: No objections from me.

Marco: 👍

Nina: 👍

Dana: 👍

Oliver: Closing thread for now. We'll follow-up on PRs and Figma.
